beijing welcomes mark carney in its campaign to sustain exports and sideline the us canadas prime minister took an important step toward reinvigorating his nations ties with china and diversifying its trade away from the us as beijing increasingly seeks to woo us allies frustrated with american protectionism mark carney is using a visit to the chinese capital to push for closer cooperation with beijing in the great hall of the people chinese premier li qiang hailed the recent turnaround of relations between beijing and the uss northern neighbor with both sides stressing opportunities to bolster trade as they seek to move beyond years of tensions hosting carney is part of a charm offensive by china which has sought to present itself as a stabilizing force and upholder of the international order at a moment of deep uncertainty from venezuela to iran as barriers to trade rise globally beijing has been especially determined to keep open the export markets on which its economy relies carney a former goldman sachs dealmaker and central banker in canada and the uk has argued that his countrys longstanding close economic relationship with the us is now over as president trump imposes tariffs and other obstacles that requires carney said canada to build deeper ties with other markets without naming the us a statement from carneys office after thursdays meeting said he and li discussed challenges impacting international trade and global supply chains and the opportunities for canada and china to cooperate trade with china however wont come close to replacing the us as canadas key source of growth though china is already canadas secondlargest trading partner with twoway trade of about 80 billion over the past 12 months that pales in comparison to the roughly 1 trillion in uscanada commerce over the same period beijing and ottawa both appear ready to stabilize ties after years of tensions that date to canadas 2018 arrest on a us extradition request of a senior huawei technologies executive china detained two canadians for nearly three years until 2021 when the us allowed huaweis chief financial officer meng wanzhou to return home carney is one of several leaders of us allies to visit china recently following trips by french president emmanuel macron in december and south korean president lee jae myung earlier this month beijing has used each opportunity to promote its vision of a world less dominated by washington yet its initiatives continue to face deep skepticism in the west in part owing to chinas support for russia and north korea before carneys trip senior canadian officials tried to temper expectations about its outcomes officials said it was unlikely the two countries would reach an agreement to resolve a trade row involving hefty tariffs on canadian agricultural products and chinesemade electric vehicles chinas ambassador to canada has said beijing would ditch a 76 tariff on canola seed in exchange for canada abandoning its 100 tariff on chinese evs carneys office said thursday that the two sides had signed memorandums of understanding covering energy combating crime and other issues providing the foundation for a new strategic partnership the canadian prime minister is expected to meet chinese leader xi jinping on friday chinas huge trade surpluses with many western countries have hindered its efforts to lure them away from the us beijing said this week that its global trade surplus hit a record of nearly 12 trillion last year exports to canada rose just over 3 last year while imports by china of canadian goods fell by more than 10 according to official chinese data carney faces geopolitical and domestic constraints in trying to deepen economic ties with china his efforts could annoy the trump administration and disrupt talks on renewing the existing north american trade pact known as usmca said former canadian diplomats and foreignpolicy analysts the trump administrations nationalsecurity strategy calls for washington with help from allies such as canada to push out or greatly reduce the influence of nonhemispheric competitors from the region the strategy reshapes us expectations of allies reframes global economic competition and redefines hemispheric security in ways that will constrain canadas policy space with china said vina nadjibulla vice president of research and strategy at the asiapacific foundation of canada polling indicates canadians view the chinese government with skepticism only 28 of canadians have a positive view of china according to polling done late last year from the angus reid institute versus 59 who view the country unfavorably the angus reid polling indicates that canadians would rather see ottawa deepen economic ties with europe and mexico over china

6 months into ownership my experience so far lets start with the truck last summer i came across some tantalizing lease deals for 25 xlt srs id been contemplating trying an ev for a couple of years but was unable to find something that would tick enough boxes to make it a smart decision for me i made a call to my local dealer to see if they could source one and one week later i had a lightning in the driveway now lets go over my experience so far from the beginning first things first ive owned a few f150s the earliest being a 2010 and without factoring range limitations this is by far the best truck ive ever owned pros very quiet in the cab very cheap to run between 1020 in monthly electricity costs the frunk is fantastic though i often get some very confused looks when i open the hood to throw my groceries in the power is instantaneous and intoxicating stepping on the pedal from a stop always gives the passengers a surprise nothing beats the instant torque of an ev conssmall annoyances its fairly loud on the outside in the cold the heat pump makes a noise comparable to a diesel engine at high idle ford dropped the ball on the software engineering for the app its garbage unreliable and poorly designed winter range drops to about 250km with highway driving a possibly less in high winds though my commute is 20km and the nearest town is 30km so 99 of my driving is unaffected by range limitations the climate control sucks at dealing with humidity im constantly cycling between auto and max defrost to keep the windows from icing up ford could have done a better job engineering the hvac to deal with that when i leased the lightning i made the decision to keep my previous truck a 2009 nissan titan first because its my plow truck and second just in case i need to drive somewhere beyond my range with no mobile charging stations which is a very realistic situation where i live in rural northern ontario im happy to report that my titan has not left the driveway since i got the lightning meaning it almost fully suits my needs in closing this is a fantastic vehicle and if a range comparable to its ice counterpart could be achieved it would fully replace my titan im disappointed that ford has discontinued it but understand the political landscape in the usa is not ev friendly

the copper market and copper quest exploration copper has reemerged as one of the most strategically important commodities in the global economy as electrification decarbonization and infrastructure renewal accelerate coppers role as a foundational industrial metal is increasingly in focus against this backdrop explorationstage companies are positioning themselves to address a growing supply gap including copper quest exploration inc copper market structural demand growth copper demand is being driven by longterm structural trends rather than shortterm cycles the energy transition alone is reshaping consumption patterns with electric vehicles renewable power generation and grid expansion all requiring significantly more copper than legacy systems electric vehicles use roughly two to four times more copper than internal combustion engine vehicles renewable energy systems such as wind and solar are substantially more copperintensive than fossilfuelbased power generation global grid expansion and modernization are required to support electrification further increasing copper demand industry forecasts widely point to sustained demand growth over the coming decade with multiple studies highlighting the risk of a structural copper supply deficit emerging later this decade supply constraints and the emerging gap while demand continues to rise copper supply faces mounting constraints new discoveries have become rarer permitting timelines longer and capital requirements higher many of the worlds largest copper mines are aging with declining grades and increasing costs average copper grades at major producing mines have fallen steadily over the past two decades bringing a new copper mine into production can take more than 10 years from discovery to first production political risk environmental regulation and community engagement challenges continue to slow project development this combination of rising demand and constrained supply underpins the strategic importance of new exploration and development projects why exploration matters in the copper cycle exploration companies play a critical role in replenishing the global copper pipeline earlystage discoveries made today will determine supply availability in the 2030s and beyond as a result jurisdictions with established infrastructure stable regulatory frameworks and access to capital are increasingly attractive for copper exploration north america in particular has gained attention as governments and industries prioritize domestic and allied supply chains for critical minerals company portfolio of explorationstage assets across established mining jurisdictions targeting systems with potential for largescale mineralization copper quests strategy centers on identifying and acquiring projects with geological characteristics consistent with coppergold and coppermolybdenum porphyry systems which are among the most important sources of global copper supply the company trades under the following tickers cse cqx otcqb imimf frankfurt 3mx recent corporate activity copper quest has remained active on the corporate and project development front announcing a series of transactions and updates aimed at expanding and strengthening its asset base acquisition and option agreements on coppergold and coppermolybdenum projects in canada and the united states completion of financing tranches to support exploration and corporate activities ongoing evaluation and advancement of acquired assets through technical review and earlystage exploration planning these activities reflect a strategy focused on portfolio growth and optionality within a strengthening copper market market positioning and outlook as coppers role in the global economy continues to expand exploration companies such as copper quest operate at the earliest stage of the value chain while exploration carries inherent risk it also offers leverage to longterm copper fundamentals if discoveries are made and advanced successfully for investors and industry participants the copper markets longterm dynamics place increasing emphasis on exploration success jurisdictional quality and disciplined capital allocation bottom line the copper market is being shaped by powerful structural forces tied to electrification energy transition and infrastructure renewal at the same time supply constraints and declining grades are tightening the longterm outlook within this environment copper quest exploration inc represents one participant seeking to position itself at the exploration end of the copper supply chain where future discoveries will be critical to meeting global demand

i edit video footage for the news i saw something unsettling part 1 threads its been almost a day since i watched that footage despite all efforts including medication relaxing music and counting sheep i couldnt sleep instead ive spent the night scouring the web for any information on what i saw but found nothing a bit about myself call me brian im from massachusetts im 33 years old and i work for an online news agency as a video editor my job is to edit transcribe and analyze recorded video from any source to make it suitable to be published i live in a single bedroom apartment near boston since the pandemic i work at home i prefer that over toxic office politics moved out of my old 3 bedroom apartment after breaking up with my girlfriend maryann to get this place that wasthree or four years ago cant remember exactly we had plans of getting engaged but things got in the way i sorry im rambling yesterday at around 1020 am standard time the agency sent me new footage to work on i still worked on the previous one which was security cam footage of a jewelry store that was robbed at gunpoint i enhanced the footage to show details about the perpetrators clothes and the gun he held the storys out now when i finally got around to work on the new footage around half an hour later i realized that these were 3 separate video files in one folder one was a 42 minute long bodycam footage the second was a 20 minute police dashcam footage and the third was a recording from a security cam that went for 5 hours i decided to watch the bodycam first now at this point i am going to copy and paste the transcription of the entire footage here and describe the scenes as good as i can you may not find anything i describe here on the internet only i have the video and the agency hasnt seen it tuesday january 13 2026 153 pm standard time florida address omitted the scene started with the pov of a police officer exiting his cruiser from the drivers side he casually strolled over to a grey ford pickup truck that had pulled over to the side of the road in front of him cars whizzed by the trucks windows were lightly tinted and closed and the truck bed seemed to have been covered the officer knocked on the window and the driver rolled it down inside were two men a younger man in presumably his late 20s dressed in a lacoste shirt and who was the driver and an older man dressed in a suit in what i would guess his 40s based on the salt and pepper hair and weathered skin sitting in the passenger seat both men looked nervous driver howdy officer what can we do for you officer howdy i pulled you over cause you guys were going 80 mph in a 70 mph zone im gonna have to see your license and registration please the young man nodded and produced the required documents he sweated profusely despite the high possibility that the ac was on and wiped his face with a handkerchief while the older man fixated on the windshield with an empty stare the officer walked back to his cruiser entered their personal data into the mobile data terminal saw nothing wrong and returned to the truck handing the papers back to the driver officer nothing wrong there gotta watch the speed limit next time the officer paused and appeared to look intently at the men officer is there a problem you look a bit on edge driver no officer were having a job appointment and were just late officer nodded care to show what youve got in the back the young mans body language tensed driver no its nothing just some electrical equipment that we dont wanna get wet officer get wet on a sunny day before the men could react the officer walked to the back of the truck to inspect the bed just as he put a hand on the cover the pickups driver floored it and sped away cursing the officer jumped into his cruiser and gave chase the next 15 minutes or so were just a view of the steering wheel as the bodycam kept recording so i opened the dashcam footage which started to play when the siren was activated for the next 4 minutes the officer slowly gained on the speeding truck while radioing for backup the truck merged into the interstate highway and sped up waving in and out of traffic then it suddenly left the interstate and swerved into a smaller highway with iron guardrails on both sides the officer was almost close enough to attempt a pit maneuver but the truck sped up again however just a few moments later the driver apparently lost control over the vehicle causing it to swerve to the shoulder tilt to the right almost roll over and smash its cabin against the guardrail sparks flew everywhere a loose stretch of guardrail impaled the cabin through the windshield and shot out the back window as the momentum dragged the truck along the metal barrier before it came to a stop and rested on 4 wheels again switching to bodycam again the officer leaped out of the cruiser and ran to the wrecked truck peering through the drivers side window the driver was clearly dead the guardrail practically bisected him from the shoulder across the chest since the view of the passenger was obstructed by the stretch of guardrail that acted like an unwanted barrier between them the officer ran to the passenger side and the older mans head was missing not a clean cut by any means torn flesh and jagged bone was where his neck used to be the scene was gruesome it was the worst i ever saw in my 8 year long experience working for the media on top of that i prided myself for having seen it all and being completely desensitized i remembered my hubris as i ran to the bathroom and emptied my stomach into the toilet after a few minutes of recovery and making myself some cereals i returned to watching the officer moved from the passenger window to the back of the truck while radioing for rescue teams and a tow truck he now inspected the back and it seems like the bed had been modified the plastic rim of the bed liner was gone either it was cut off or the liner had been removed completely the cover was also not made of plastic but steel the officer tried to push it open and pulled on the tailgate but they wont budge upon closer inspection it turned out that the bed along the cover and the tailgate had been welded shut end of footage intrigued by the horrific accident i googled ford pickup truck accident florida not finding anything resembling what i saw i proceeded to watch the security cam footage this was when things got weird so much so that i lost sleep over it the footage showed a yard of some sort it had a dirt ground with sand and rocks and was surrounded by what looked like piles of sandbags nothing happened for over 4 hours so i fast forwarded until i saw movement at the 2 hour and 12 minute mark a forklift came into view carrying a severely damaged vehicle i recognized it to be the same pickup truck from the accident with the guardrail the forklift placed it in the center of the yard and backed away a few minutes later a remote controlled robot commonly used to handle explosives approached the truck its arm extended to the truck bed and started to cut the tailgate open a shower of sparks flew from the spinning blade i could imagine the sensational headlines the following day should the truck contain an ied or biological or chemical weapons the robot made a vertical cut almost across the entire height of the tailgate and proceeds to cut horizontally a rectangle big enough to peer in or let anything thats inside fall out i suppose after the robot made its final cut and the rectangular piece of metal fell to the ground something that i cant explain happened the footage started to glitch out it lost color momentarily and was interspersed with thick lines of static static across the entire screen for a few seconds in between the jittery static lines i could see something threads many of them maybe thousands or millions of them black extremely long hair like strands they shot out of the hole and spread across the ground in all directions with incredible speed they just kept coming out of that truck bed they engulfed the entire vehicle all of this didnt last longer than a few seconds then the video quality returned to normal nothing happened the truck was still there so was the robot but the threads were gone i heard a noise so i adjusted the volume it sounded like shouting screaming and gunshots fairly distant end of footage i sat in shocked silence for an indeterminate period i lost track of how long i sat there finally i managed to google the florida police department website and look for a police report finding nothing i contacted them to send me one im still waiting for a response i googled every detail i noticed in the video including lacoste ford florida address where it happened and i found something on a post on 4chan there was a link with no description i didnt want to catch a virus so i opened the link in a vm the link took me to a mp4 file on mega it was secured with a password i thought of entering the trucks plate number and it worked i downloaded the file onto the vm and watched the footage was shaky as if recorded from a cellphone whoever was recording ran wildly and panted clearly out of breath the footage was extremely blurry due to it being so shaky so i put it through my video editing software where i could slow it frame by frame and enhance the quality of each frame to a high degree of clarity it appeared to be a hallway of sorts white walls with a green stripe doors on each side some were open some not the floor was covered in papers at one point inside one of the doorways someone laid on the floor a person with a police uniform which seemed a couple sizes too big the body was positioned halfway through the door i couldnt see the face clearly after refining the footage some more i recoiled in abject horror the officer wasnt just dead heor she wasemaciated the body looked mummified as if every last drop of moisture had been sucked out eyes sunken into their pits skin stretched over bone teeth grinning when the camera panned for just a fraction of a second to what was behind the running man i paused the blurry footage looked like a person levitating in the air with a cloud of smoke surrounding them was that what they were running from after enhancing the frame greatly my stomach dropped completely i already felt uneasy but this pushed over the edge behind the running man was another police officer apparently dead and lifted in the air by what looked like thousands of black hairlike strands that threaded themselves through his entire body like a knitting project end of footage the shock after watching this has endured through the night i honestly dread any more footage sent my way today at the same time i want to get to the bottom of this but how i cant report it because everyone at the agency thinks im either crazy or fabricated something with ai to get paid higher this wasnt ai it was tooreal we have deepfake detection tools and i used them it wasnt a deepfake what was thathair thing whatever it was its free now if anyone has an idea feel free to comment ill keep you posted on updates ill label this part 1 just in case there has to be more to this

how to reduce your carbon footprint 10 or more in 2026 climate change is shaped by large systems policies and industries but those systems are not separate from daily life they respond to what people choose normalize and demand at scale when millions of individuals shift habits and preferences markets move infrastructure follows and political will strengthens a ten percent reduction in personal carbon footprint may sound modest but across households and communities it becomes transformative the goal is not perfection or sacrifice but choosing actions that are realistic repeatable and easy to sustain especially when life gets busy oneanddone shifts that reduce emissions every day some of the most effective carbon reductions happen once and then continue automatically switching your electricity supply to a renewable option through your utility or community energy program is often one of the largest single reductions a household can make requiring only a short signup and no lifestyle change if available opting into timeofuse plans and shifting major electricity use to offpeak hours further lowers emissions by aligning demand with cleaner energy on the grid replacing old incandescent or halogen bulbs with leds installing a smart thermostat and sealing obvious air leaks around doors and windows are similarly simple actions that reduce energy use year after year without ongoing effort choosing an efficient appliance when an old one fails rather than upgrading early locks in longterm savings while avoiding unnecessary manufacturing emissions even small steps like installing lowflow showerheads or faucet aerators quietly reduce both water and energy use for decades lowcarbon food choices that dont require perfection food is one of the easiest places to cut emissions without tracking numbers shifting toward more plantbased meals even a few days a week can deliver a meaningful reduction while improving health and lowering grocery costs making this easy matters so many people find success by anchoring habits such as defaulting to plantbased breakfasts and lunches or choosing one or two fully plantbased dinner nights each week reducing food waste is equally powerful and often overlooked planning meals freezing leftovers and keeping a visible eat first shelf in the fridge prevents food from becoming methane in landfills buying seasonal produce more often and choosing whole foods over heavily processed items reduces emissions tied to manufacturing and packaging without requiring strict rules transportation habits that reduce miles without feeling restrictive transportation emissions fall quickly when driving becomes more intentional rather than automatic one of the most effective loweffort strategies is clustering errands appointments and social plans onto the same day or route so trips stack instead of multiplying many people find it helpful to designate one or two out days each week and protect the rest for walking biking or staying local when possible choosing remote work days carpooling hybrid schedules or virtual meetings eliminates entire trips rather than trying to optimize them for short distances defaulting to walking or biking not only cuts emissions but often saves time once parking and traffic are factored in keeping tires properly inflated and driving smoothly are small habits that reduce fuel use without changing where you go when replacing a vehicle becomes necessary choosing a smaller more efficient model or an electric option locks in longterm reductions buying habits that slow carbon without feeling like deprivation much of household carbon comes from how often we replace things extending the life of what you already own is one of the most underappreciated climate actions repairing maintaining and reusing items delays the energyintensive process of manufacturing replacements making this easier can be as simple as keeping basic repair tools visible learning one new repair skill per year or choosing repairable designs when purchasing new items buying used for furniture clothing and electronics dramatically reduces embodied emissions while often saving money when buying new choosing fewer bettermade items and pausing before impulse purchases reduces the volume of goods moving through your life and the emissions tied to them to reset out of control spending habits try limiting purchases to essentialsonly for 30 days home and lifestyle rhythms that cut energy use daily habits dont need to be tracked to be effective letting indoor temperatures drift slightly with the seasons dressing for the weather and using fans or layered bedding reduce heating and cooling demand without discomfort linedrying clothes when possible washing in cold water and running full loads are loweffort defaults that quickly add up turning devices fully off rather than leaving them on standby and using smart power strips to shut down multiple items at once makes energy savings automatic spending more time outdoors or in naturally lit spaces also reduces reliance on artificial lighting and climate control while improving wellbeing work and digital choices that shape larger systems work patterns influence emissions more than many people realize advocating for remote or hybrid options flexible schedules or fourday workweeks reduces commuting and building energy use at scale choosing adlight platforms reducing unnecessary streaming and keeping devices longer lowers energy demand in data centers and manufacturing while individual digital actions may seem small collectively they signal demand for more efficient lowercarbon infrastructure social and community habits that multiply impact carbon reduction becomes easier when its shared talking openly about simple changes youve made hosting plantforward meals carpooling to regular activities or sharing tools and equipment with neighbors reduces duplication and normalizes lowercarbon living these actions quietly influence others without preaching creating social permission for change when people see lowcarbon choices as convenient and satisfying rather than restrictive adoption accelerates reducing your carbon footprint by ten percent does not require a dramatic overhaul of your life it comes from stacking a handful of onetime decisions with a set of habits that are easy to remember and repeat when enough people make these shifts they dont just reduce emissions directly they reshape markets policies and infrastructure personal action is not a substitute for systemic change but it is one of the forces that makes systemic change possible

zermatt with three generations new years week trip report im about two years behind on writing this up but i wanted to share our week in zermatt over new years 20232024 with nine family members spanning three generations our youngest was one year old our oldest in their late 60s and we had a mix of skiers and nonskiers since then weve skied in courchevel the dolomites spent a few weeks in lech in the summer and just got back from banfflake louise over the 20252026 holidays and of course colorado and utah in our own backyard those trip reports will come eventually im working through the backlog but zermatt was our first european ski trip as a family and set the bar high we started looking at hotels back in the spring prior which turned out to not be overkill at all most of the better properties require 1012 night minimum stays during peak periods and a lot of them sell out before they even publish their rates online its common for the same families to book the same rooms year after year we wanted 7 nights and got lucky when la ginabelle agreed to it after we emailed them directly the whole booking process for european ski hotels is bizarre if youre used to the us some only allow checkin on certain days of the week many dont have english websites and the rates dont show up on some booking sites until surprisingly late we looked at courchevel st moritz and verbier pretty seriously before settling on zermatt the altitude was a big factor for us zermatt tops out at 12792 feet which meant we had a better shot at decent snow conditions in late december and early january compared to lower resorts the ikon pass access sealed it though we got five days of skiing with zero blackout dates over new years week which you absolutely cannot do at most us resorts on a base pass kids under nine also ski free in zermatt which saved us a meaningful amount of money getting there the journey from zurich airport to zermatt takes about four hours we hired a private mercedes sprinter van for the nine of us plus all our luggage on the way there it was convenient walking out of the airport and having someone waiting for us but no bathroom on board of course we were cramped with all our ski gear and you feel every hairpin turn on the way back we took the train from zermatt to geneva and i wish we had just done that both directions the train station in zermatt is right in the center of town really convenient you have actual bathrooms the kids could walk around when they got restless and the whole experience was better they even have little kids play areas on some of the train cars we paid extra for first class and honestly not sure it was worth the premium our flight timing forced us to overnight in geneva on the way out id try to avoid that layover if you can make the flight schedules work but sometimes you cant one thing that surprised me about zermatt is that cars really arent allowed in the village id read this but didnt fully understand what it meant permitted electric vehicles can drop you off and most hotels will send an electric shuttle to pick you up at the dropoff point if you drive yourself to the area you park in tsch which is about five kilometers away and take a train into zermatt the whole village runs on electric taxis and buses which adds to the charm but also means the taxi drivers feel like theyre constantly racing against the clock walking around with two toddlers while these electric taxis whipped past us was legitimately nerveracking i kept wishing there were separate pedestrian lanes the mountain i knew zermatt was big before we got there but the statistics dont really prepare you for the reality the vertical drop is 7477 feet revelstoke in british columbia is considered massive by north american standards and its 5620 feet the longest ski run in zermatt is 22 kilometers which ranks second in the world youre constantly looking around and being reminded of just how huge the landscape is the infrastructure to move people around the mountain is completely different from anything ive seen in north america youre taking trains between different zones of the mountain riding through tunnels carved into the rock taking cable cars and funiculars skiing by train was a first for us and it quickly became a normal part of our day navigating the terrain multiple locals agreed with us that the rockies generally have better skiing especially if youre after powder we didnt come across much tree skiing either we ski in colorado a lot and love it but zermatt offers something different the long groomed cruisers paired with the food the culture the scene and having the matterhorn in view constantly made it a really unique experience theres plenty of offpiste skiing available but because it was early in the season and conditions werent in their prime yet we were advised to stick to groomed runs we decided to spend one day skiing from zermatt into italy there was definitely enough terrain left to explore on the swiss side but we thought it would be fun to ski to italy for the day or maybe we just wanted to be able to say we did it either way we paid about 50 chf extra per person and dont regret it we hired a guide through european snowsport for that day a guide isnt strictly necessary but we were so glad we did it he helped us maximize our time on the best terrain and navigate the maze of lifts trams cable cars and gondolas without him we would have spent half the day staring at the ski map trying to figure out where to go next our guide was excellent he spoke perfect english and spent the day sharing stories about zermatts history and geography while leading us to the best runs for each time of day midmorning he took us to an italian hut where we had espressos before continuing the whole experience felt special every time you look at the matterhorn you see it differently different angles different cloud formations different light throughout the day as you work your way up the mountain you pass the gorner glacier which is the largest glacier in the alps these massive prehistoric ice formations have this incredible turquoise hue its the kind of scenery that makes you stop and just stare ski school we put our kids in ski school for five days through european snowsport our youngest was three and a half and did half days our son was six and did full days the instructors were friendly and the kids took to them right away i should mention that many of the local ski school operations dont accept children under four which is why we went with european snowsport specifically they did a great job because ski schools in europe are privately owned and operated rather than monopolized by the resort they dont have the same facilities you see in the us we dropped the kids off at a predetermined meeting point at the bottom of a lift rather than at a dedicated ski school building it wasnt a problem just different from what were used to the price difference compared to the us is honestly shocking five full days of lessons for oliver seven hours per day with lunch included cost 875 i looked up the equivalent at vail just to see five days there would have been 2665 and thats only for 55 hours per day without lunch the fact that european ski areas dont allow one operator to monopolize instruction creates actual competition which drives prices way down our ikon passes worked seamlessly at all the turnstiles without needing to stop at any pass office first the cards were already preprogrammed to get us through that was a nice surprise where we stayed we seriously considered renting a chalet to keep everyone together in one space there are both catered and selfcatered options available but we ultimately went with a hotel and stayed at la ginabelle which is a fourstar property there were several reasons this worked out better for us than a chalet would have the spa and wellness facilities were perfect they had steam rooms multiple types of saunas an indooroutdoor pool and hot tubs after a long day on the mountain this was exactly what we needed the kids were even more into it than we were the pool became a daily destination for them to burn off excess energy before dinner breakfast was included in our stay which mattered more than i expected we had big lunches and dinners booked most days so we wanted something quick and light in the morning but still good la ginabelle had a table reserved for us every morning with a continental buffet plus fresh eggs and pancakes made to order they had a selfserve juicer where we made ginger carrot and apple juice every morning there was also fresh honey that you scraped directly from a honeycomb which the kids loved location was crucial for us we wanted to be within walking distance of both town and the ski lifts the kids ski school met at the sunnegga funicular which was about a fiveminute walk from la ginabelle at a toddlers meandering pace we rarely needed to call a taxi or take the bus because almost everything was within a 515 minute walk our room was set up perfectly for a family we had a large king bedroom plus a living space on the first level and a kids bunk room up on the second story in my experience its hard to find something equivalent in the us without booking two separate rooms the kids club was probably the biggest gamechanger la ginabelle offered this free of charge and our kids loved it so much that it became part of our daily routine wed ski hit the pool do kids club then go to dinner the club was open until 10pm and they served dinner to the kids there which meant the adults could go out to eat early without them before anyone judges we spent an enormous amount of time with the kids on this trip including some very long and emotional travel days having childcare available helped us manage some otherwise impossible logistics and honestly helped us feel more balanced and rested during what was a pretty intense week the owner of la ginabelle and his family are very present in running the hotel throughout our stay wed see him putting logs on the fire in the lobby clearing plates in the restaurant and greeting guests at the front desk his childrens names and birthdates are handpainted on the lobby fireplace one night our babysitter turned out to be his daughter this is a proper hotel with maybe 30 or 40 rooms not some tiny bed and breakfast where that level of personal involvement would be expected there was something really wholesome about it that contributed to our overall experience the finishes and decor were true to the fourstar rating not ultramodern or fivestar luxury but everything was clean wellappointed charming and authentic the service breakfast and location all felt fivestar to us though if we were to go back id probably stay at la ginabelle again for other options worth considering mont cervin palace also has a kids club which is not common in zermatt many hotels there arent particularly kidfriendly at all for properties with modern design we like cervo and omnia for classic luxury right in town grand hotel zermatterhof and mont cervin palace are amazing restaurants the onmountain lunch chalets were honestly one of the highlights of the trip the experience is so different from the overpriced overcooked cafeteria burger you reluctantly eat at us ski resorts that it barely feels like the same category of dining on our first day we took the gornergrat train up to alphitta the food was very good and the setting was stunning but we ended up preferring some of the other places we tried later in the week zum see was a really fun lunch stop you ski through a small historic village to get there the chicken noodle soup was excellent chez vrony might have been my favorite the vrony burger and meat and cheese plate were both great and vrony herself greeted us when we arrived the views from there are outstanding we also skied into italy one day and had lunch at chalet etoile in cervinia the menu was extensive and we ordered family style to try a bunch of things nothing disappointed for dinner brasserie uno was our michelinstarred meal its a very small chefowned restaurant with a tasting menu you could feel the passion not just from the chef but from the entire staff throughout the meal the whole experience felt intimate and special grampis became our goto familyfriendly spot in town its loud the acoustics are terrible which actually worked in our favor because it drowned out any whining or crying from the kids the pizza and pasta were delicious we had the carbonella with charcoal pizza dough and the raviolo di brasato al barolo multiple times the salads were forgettable this is going to sound odd but we had indian food one night at golden india the mint chutney and tikka masala were excellent it seemed weird to travel all the way to zermatt for one of our favorite takeout cuisines at home but after several days of heavy swiss meat and cheese it was exactly what we needed we also went to ferdinands at the cervo hotel for a modern take on fondue it was fun a local told us that petit royal was the best bakery in town but we never made it there for heavier meatfocused dinners spycher and whymper stube were recommended to us though we didnt try them aprs the aprs scene in zermatt exists but isnt overwhelming hennu stahl was the main spot if you get there too early youll wonder where everyone is as the party doesnt really start until 330pm or later harrys bar in town is small and quaint with both indoor and outdoor spaces though the indoor area is tiny so dont expect to get a seat the scene builds there midafternoon theres a champagne bar where you can grab a glass on your way down the mountain skiing back to town which is a nice touch cervo is a cool hotel with a good happy hour scene at their outdoor patio bar we checked out paperla club one night which is a grimy loud crowded bar in town blasting music if thats your scene youll probably love it we left pretty quickly what else we did the gornergrat railway goes to the top of the mountain and has been electric since it was built in 1898 which i found incredible you can ride it with or without skis its included on the ikon pass at no additional cost and the views are worth the trip even if youre not skiing we took the kids up one day and they loved it we went to gitz gadi one evening expecting the food to be mediocre and the real draw to be the sledging afterward the food was actually excellent though we took the furi lift up had dinner with a wonderful waiter then jumped on sleds and rode them down the mountain back to town the ride took about 20 minutes and the kids talked about it for days a highlight of our trip only operates certain nights of the week and requires enough snow for the return to town by sledge theres igludorf if you want to grab fondue sausages and drinks at an actual igloo on the mountain we saw several public playgrounds scattered throughout zermatt but they were all covered in snow and didnt look appealing to us or the kids i imagine theyre great in the summer though if your hotel has a pool use it our kids went every single day and it was the perfect way for them to release energy at the end of the day before dinner what it cost a lot of people have asked us whether zermatt is expensive the answer is yes and no some things are far cheaper than highend us ski resorts others are more expensive obviously getting there from the us is costly though if youre on the east coast the difference between flying to vail and flying plus training to zermatt might actually be marginal we went during peak season over new years week so our costs were higher than they would be at other times of year lodging was 8600 for seven nights with breakfast included for comparison there are hostels and simple airbnbs available if youre working with a tighter budget lift tickets through ikon covered five days of skiing for us kids under nine skied free day tickets in zermatt and most alps resorts are far cheaper than in the us if youre not on a pass already we rented ski equipment from bayard sport which has multiple locations around town we chose the one at the bottom of the sunnegga lift for convenience and proximity to where the kids ski school met prices were comparable to the us maybe slightly cheaper food was objectively expensive but honestly quite comparable to highend us ski resorts while the prices stung a little we had so many wonderful dining experiences that we never felt ripped off the restaurants were charming the staff was authentic and friendly and the food was excellent a lot of it was sourced locally too we found cocktail prices to be about on par with what wed expect in the us good italian and swiss wines were cheaper local taxis were expensive they charged a minimum of 13 chf even for a threeminute ride across town for that reason we walked whenever possible theres a reliable and frequent local bus system with routes and pickup times available on google maps which made it easy to figure out random observations the scale of everything is just different the amount of infrastructure required to shuttle skiers around this mountain tunnels cable cars funiculars trams lifts trains is fascinating and unlike anything weve experienced in north america we didnt come across too many americans the ikon pass seems to draw some but its not overrun with us tourists by any means this was 2 years ago though and maybe thats changed whats next since this trip weve checked off courchevel and les trois valles spent time in the dolomites summered in lech austria and most recently skied banff and lake louise over the 20252026 holidays kitzbhel and japan are still high on the list wed also love to get back to zermatt in the summerweve heard its spectacular trip reports for all of those are coming im just perpetually behind on writing these things up the research and planning for european ski destinations is just completely different from booking a trip to vail or park city the minimum stays specific checkin days rates that dont publish until months out hotels selling out before going public its a lot layer in the logistics of planning in advance required over the festive weeks and it can feel like a full time job
